ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the parabola $y=-x^{2}+bx+c$ intersects the x-axis at points $A(2, 0)$ and $B(-4, 0)$. Determine the axis of symmetry and the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $y=-x^2-2x+8=-\left(x+1\right)^2+9$,\\
therefore the axis of symmetry is the line $x=-1$, and the coordinates of the vertex are $\boxed{(-1,9)}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the parabola $y=-x^{2}+bx+c$ intersects the x-axis at points $A(2, 0)$ and $B(-4, 0)$. Determine the axis of symmetry and the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a parabola opening downward, intersecting the x-axis at the left point B and the right point A; in the figure there is also a vertical dashed line passing through the highest point of the parabola, indicating the axis of symmetry. The problem text gives the two x-axis intersection points as A(2,0) and B(-4,0), and the parabola form as y=-x^2+bx+c. Because the axis of symmetry of the parabola is located at the midpoint of the two x-axis intersection points, the axis of symmetry is x=(2+(-4))/2=-1. Also because the leading coefficient is -1, and the roots are x=2 and x=-4, the function can be written as y=-(x-2)(x+4). Substituting the x-coordinate of the axis of symmetry x=-1 gives y=-((-1)-2)((-1)+4)=-(-3)(3)=9. Therefore the vertex coordinate is (-1,9).

Use the fact that the axis of symmetry of a parabola lies midway between its two x-intercepts, so x=(2+(-4))/2=-1.
